items.title: Indian Mathematics: Engaging with the World from Ancient to Modern Times
items.note: Survey including the Kerala school, restating the case that Jesuit intermediaries plausibly carried series results to Europe.

items.title: Karaṇapaddhati of Putumana Somayājī
items.who: V. Pai, K. Ramasubramanian, M. S. Sriram and M. D. Srinivas
items.venue: Springer, Sources and Studies in the History of Mathematics
items.note: Critical edition and translation of a later Kerala computational manual, widening the documented corpus of the school.

items.title: The Mathematics of India: Concepts, Methods, Connections
items.note: Reconstructs the conceptual development of Kerala calculus-like methods and discusses their relation to European analysis.

items.title: Jesuit Mathematics
items.note: Overview of the Jesuit mathematical curriculum and networks around Clavius, the institutional channel any transmission would have used.

items.title: Testing Ground for Jesuit Accommodation in Early Modern India: Francisco Ros SJ in Malabar (16th–17th Centuries)
items.note: Archival study of the Malabar Jesuits around Ros, documenting their linguistic and scholarly contacts in Kerala, though not mathematics.

items.title: Jost Bürgi's methods of calculating sines, and possible transmission from India
items.venue: Archive for History of Exact Sciences
items.note: Reconstructs Bürgi's sine-table algorithm and weighs whether it could derive from Indian methods; no documentary channel is identified.

items.title: The Untapped Wealth of Manuscripts on Indian Astronomy and Mathematics
items.venue: Indian Journal of History of Science
items.note: Surveys the large body of unedited Sanskrit and Malayalam astronomical manuscripts, many from Kerala, still awaiting study.

items.title: Use of the concept of derivative in the computation of vyatīpāta in two Kerala texts
items.who: V. Pai R. and M. S. Sriram
items.venue: Indian Journal of History of Science
items.note: Shows Kerala astronomers using instantaneous rates of change in a practical computation, extending the evidence for their analytical methods.

items.title: Jesuit Missions in Coastal and South India (1543–1773)
items.note: Synthesis of Jesuit missions in Kerala and the south, useful for mapping which missionaries had the access and training to acquire Kerala texts.

items.title: Tantrasaṅgraha of Nīlakaṇṭha Somayājī
items.who: K. Ramasubramanian and M. S. Sriram
items.note: Springer edition of the translation and technical commentary of Nīlakaṇṭha's 1500 treatise, a core Kerala-school text.
